headline: National Grid pole petitions granted with conditions; 10% affordable housing requirement enrolled; animal control moved to Health Department.
summary: Four National Grid pole locations were granted with conditions, and the Broadway and Eastern Avenue conduit work was tabled. Affordable housing and parking rule changes were enrolled, while a hotel height proposal and an $800,000 snow and ice budget cut went to committee.
decisions: Approved reappointments of Dr. Scoon Carrington, John Colangeli, and Dr. Qunao Singh to the Board of Health, unanimously.
Split the Broadway and Eastern Avenue underground conduit work from the National Grid petition and tabled it, so National Grid must file a new petition.
Approved National Grid pole petitions at four locations, 10-0 on roll call, with conditions and the 6 Blane pole moved to 30 ft south of pole 2023.
Referred to the Rules and Ordinance Committee a proposal to allow hotels up to six stories, not to exceed 75 feet.
Enrolled the move of the animal control officer from the Police Department to the Health Department.
Referred to the Finance Committee a $800,000 cut to the Department of Public Works FY 2027 budget for FY 2026 snow and ice costs.
Approved (ordained) changes to the zoning use table that let hospitals, restaurants, convenience stores, and other uses go in more zones, unanimously.
Approved (ordained) a new salary schedule for assistant department heads, unanimously.
Enrolled the inclusionary zoning update (Paper 335-26), lowering the affordable housing requirement from 15% to 10%, with committee amendments, by a 9-1 roll call.
Enrolled housing incentives for affordable and inclusionary projects, with height bonuses outside Residence A and parking of 1.1 spaces per market unit and 0.7 per affordable unit, 9-0 on roll call.
Approved a $157,000 transfer from Salary Reserve to accounts in a dozen departments for retroactive raises for assistant department directors, 9-0 on roll call.
Approved a $220,000 transfer from Salary Reserve to Police Salaries for a retroactive 3% cost-of-living increase for patrol officers, 9-0 on roll call.
discussion: Residents objected to a new utility pole in front of a Blane Street home. National Grid moved it 20 feet toward the corner, and said underground wiring would also need new poles there.

Members asked whether the city engineer should review the Broadway and Eastern Avenue underground work before approval. They noted the Broadway redesign is a major project that could cost $20 million or more.

Members debated lowering the affordable housing requirement for new apartments from 15% to 10%. Supporters cited building costs and interest rates; others said incentives and zoning limits matter more than the percentage.

Members discussed parking requirements for new housing, and views differed on reducing them. Some noted existing parking problems in neighborhoods; others said lower parking requirements help housing get built.
The chair ruled against splitting the inclusionary zoning paper, saying state law required the incentives to be a separate paper. A member objected that the rules were applied unevenly.
